evidence.note: Chose a monolithic 'implement model/parsers/layouts/analysis/alignment/CLI/runners all at once' patch rather than an ordered set of milestones — the opposite of dependency-staged sequencing, which then produced a compile cascade requiring module-by-module recovery.

Genuine dependency awareness: recognized SIF/GW parsers are stubbed and cause ALL analysis tests to fail at network-load time, so fixed foundational parsers first; ran a single test to find the first panic before proceeding — foundational-before-downstream reasoning.

Within the analysis_tests grouping, tackled components in dependency order (parsers → graph → cycle → alignment scoring/grouping), each sub-goal ending with a re-run of the analysis suite as the done-check (20/63 → 63/63).
After analysis passed, moved to the cli_tests suite as the next grouping, implementing CLI handlers and re-running cli tests as the completion signal — work grouped by test suite in a sensible order.

Finished with parity_tests compile fixes then cycle_property_tests / alignment layout — suite-by-suite progression, but these later groups were driven reactively by whichever tests still failed rather than a pre-declared milestone map.

reasoning: The agent consistently groups work by test suite and advances them in a defensible dependency order (parsers/model → layout → analysis → CLI → parity/property), each grouping closing with a runnable test — matching the level-5 anchor, with some genuine dependency awareness (parsers as load-time blockers) nudging slightly above it. It falls short of level 8 because there was no explicit up-front milestone plan tied to specific test groups; the sensible ordering emerged reactively after an initial monolithic 'do everything at once' patch (step 25), and per-step plans are tactical rather than milestone-defined. This places it solidly at 5.
